data.title: Steppe Gold Ltd. reports Q3 results
data.description:
• Steppe Gold Ltd. press release (STGO:CA): Net profit attributable to shareholders of the company was $37,389 for the third quarter and $56,336 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7,066 and $22,677, respectively, in 2025. 
  • Revenue increased to $86,570 in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $29,398 in the same period in 2025, reflecting higher gold sales volumes and higher realised gold prices. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue was $201,599, compared to $94,093 in the corresponding period in 2025.

data.title: U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino named new coach for Manchester United
data.description:
Manchester United has confirmed that U.S. Men’s National coach Mauricio Pochettino has been named the football club’s new manager amid hopes that the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will work his magic on 18th place Manchester.

Pochettino is credited with taking Tottenham Hotspur to the UEFA Champions League final in 2019 and winning the Ligue 1 title for Paris Saint-Germain before leaving in 2022 to later joint Chelsea the following year.

Manchester United (MANU) has had a disappointing start to the season with just one win, 4 losses, and 5 draws, making this season the worst start for the club in 40 years and putting Manchester United precariously close to relegation.

On Thursday, the club announced that an “extremely difficult conclusion was made in order to achieve our ambitions,” and Carrick was removed as manager following a meeting between director of football Jason Wilcox, CEO Omar Berrada, and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Fortunately, the disappointing performance of the club has not had a meaningful impact on Manchester United’s (MANU) share price given its three major sources of revenue (broadcasting, merchandising, and matchday). After an 18% retracement from the $24.45 high in August, MANU bounced off the 200-day moving average to recover back towards the $24 per share level.

data.title: Medline bed deaths rise to seven
data.description:
• Following an FDA alert in October regarding a fire hazard with its hospital beds that led to two deaths and 16 injuries, Medline (MDLN) upped the number of deaths associated with the issue to seven.
  • As of Nov. 8, the company also said 35 serious injuries have been reported.
  • "Medline will soon begin distributing new repair and replace Customer Guides to patients and users of all relevant Medline Brand beds, rails, mattresses and accessories, in line with previous updates," Medline said on Friday.

data.title: Xylem launches $1.5B share repurchase program
data.description:
• Xylem (XYL) on Friday announced a new share repurchase program of its common stock of up to $1.5 billion, effective immediately.
  • Repurchases may be made from time to time on the open market or in privately negotiated transactions, the company said, adding that it intends to be opportunistic in its repurchases based on market conditions and other factors and may suspend or discontinue the repurchase program at any time.
  • Press Release

data.title: Condor Resources CEO Chris Buncic to step down in December
data.description:
• Condor Resources (CN:CA) announced on Friday that President and CEO Chris Buncic will resign, effective December 23, 2026.

  • Buncic, who has led the company since April 2024, is leaving to pursue another opportunity.

  • CFO Jonathan Younie will serve as interim president and CEO until a permanent replacement is appointed.

data.title: Yiren Digital not in compliance with NYSE stock price requirement
data.description:
• Yiren Digital (YRD) said on Friday that it received a notification from the NYSE stating that it was not in compliance with the stock exchange's price requirement for continued listing.
  • The company added that it received the notification letter on October 20, 2026, and has six months to regain compliance.
  • Press Release
